content: Hey! I’m in a bit of a bind with my thesis research. I need some key papers from Nature and Science, but I can't afford the $500 for access. Have you heard of any good ways to get them without breaking the bank?

I have! There are a number of strategies that you can try to get the papers you need. First, you can check out our guide to getting papers for free. It has some great tips on how to find open access versions of papers and how to request them from libraries.

You can also try searching for the papers on Google Scholar or other similar platforms. Many researchers post their papers online for free, and you may be able to find the paper you need this way.

Finally, you can try contacting the researchers who wrote the paper and asking them if they have a copy they can share with you. This can be a bit more time-consuming, but it's a great way to build relationships with researchers in your field.

I hope these tips help! Good luck with your research.

Thanks for the suggestions! I did think about reaching out to the authors, and that might work for some of them. But I really want to avoid using Sci-Hub. I get that some people do it, but it feels wrong to me, especially since a lot of researchers work hard to publish their work. I want to be responsible and respect their efforts. 

Do you know if there are any specific preprint servers or platforms where I might find these papers?

Yes, there are a few different options. One option is to search for the paper on a preprint server like arXiv or bioRxiv. These platforms are often used by researchers to share their work before it's been peer-reviewed and published in a journal. So, it's possible that you'll find the paper you need on one of these platforms.

Another option is to use a platform like ResearchGate or Academia.edu. These platforms allow researchers to share their papers and other research materials for free. You can search for the paper you need on these platforms and see if anyone has posted it.

Finally, you can try contacting the researchers who wrote the paper and asking them if they have a copy they can share with you. This can be a bit more time-consuming, but it's a great way to build relationships with researchers in your field.

I hope these tips help! Good luck with your research.

Hopefully, I can find what I need without having to resort to anything sketchy. Thanks for your help!

I hope this helps! Good luck with your research.
